one_line_pitch_to_sam: It's a sword-fighting game where it says you slashed your friend 'into a nap', and there's a bench that launches you into a pool, but you run out of stuff in twenty minutes.

moments.why: Spawning onto a grey floor was just the start; nothing about it stuck.
Running around was just how you got places.
The dummy standing there confused Kai for three seconds and was gone.
The first punch felt good at the time but the sword replaced it straight away.
The combo launch got a grin, then got buried under everything with Robin.
Kicking each other off the tower right before the bell was a huge shared laugh.
Hitting each other blurred into the kills; the shield confusion was never understood.
They only remember that you get a sword, and that there is only the one.
Slashing was the whole fight so no single slash stands out.
Kai recalls setting a dummy record, mostly as the point where there was nothing left to do.
The 'into a nap' line and the 7-3 score are what they brag and argue about.
The board writing the rivalry down thrilled Robin, but the empty 'that's it?' ending is what Kai complains about.
Kai landed one parry and felt like a genius, so they brag about it.
Robin's sneak attack was their first kill, though it never worked a second time.
The late, silent laugh and salute fell flat and vanished.
'No emote called flex' was mildly amusing for a second.
The game announcing 'left hanging' in the feed was funny and the real high five was a shared moment.
'Danced on Kai' stuck as a taunt, and the missing music stuck as a complaint.
Moving cancelling the dance was not noticed as a thing.
A timed race with a record Kai owns, and unfinished business getting under five seconds.
Nobody expected the superhero landing, so it surprised them both.
Swimming on its own was 'just blue' and is remembered only as boring.
Loudest moment of the night, plus a one-stud record Kai can never beat and still fumes about.
'Fell off the world' was funny but the long grey run to get there bored Kai into tabbing out.
'Waved bye-bye to Kai' genuinely tilted Kai, so Robin will never let it go.
Robin's accidental parry got a laugh then but Kai's own parry is the one that gets retold.
